sentences.zh: =杜黃裳=杜黃裳，字遵素，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Huangchang — Du Huangchang, styled Zunsu, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang, styled Zunsu, came from Duling in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 登進士第、宏辭科，杜鴻漸深器重之。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and the hongci examination; Du Hongjian greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He earned degrees in the jinshi and hongci examinations, and Du Hongjian held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 為郭子儀朔方從事，子儀入朝，令黃裳主留務於朔方。

translations.literal: He served as an aide in Guo Ziyi's Shuofang command; when Ziyi went to court, he ordered Huangchang to manage remaining affairs in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He became an aide on Guo Ziyi's Shuofang staff; when Guo Ziyi proceeded to the capital, he left Huangchang in charge of affairs at Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 邠將李懷光與監軍陰謀代子儀，乃為偽詔書，欲誅大將溫儒雅等。

translations.literal: The Binzhou general Li Huai'guang and the army supervisor secretly plotted to replace Ziyi; they forged an imperial edict intending to execute the great generals Wen Ruya and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Binzhou commander Li Huai'guang conspired with the army supervisor to supplant Guo Ziyi and forged an edict calling for the execution of senior generals such as Wen Ruya.

sentences.zh: 黃裳立辨其偽，以告懷光，懷光流汗伏罪。

translations.literal: Huangchang immediately identified it as forged and reported this to Huai'guang; Huai'guang sweated and submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchang at once recognized the forgery and confronted Huai'guang, who broke into a sweat and confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 諸將有難制者，黃裳矯子儀命盡出之，數月而亂不作。

translations.literal: Among the generals there were some hard to control; Huangchang forged orders in Ziyi's name and had them all transferred out, and for several months no disturbance arose.
translations.idiomatic: For unruly officers he issued transfers in Guo Ziyi's name and removed them from post; for months no mutiny followed.

sentences.zh: 後入為臺省官，為裴延齡所惡，十年不遷。

translations.literal: Later he entered service as an official of the Censorate and Secretariat offices; Pei Yanling bore him ill will, and for ten years he received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in the central censorial and secretariat offices but was detested by Pei Yanling and went ten years without advancement.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，為太常卿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he became Director of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenyuan reign he was appointed Director of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 王叔文之竊權，黃裳終不造其門。

translations.literal: When Wang Shuwen usurped power, Huangchang never once visited his door.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Shuwen's seizure of power, Huangchang never set foot at his house.

sentences.zh: 嘗語其子婿韋執誼，令率百官請皇太子監國，執誼遽曰：「丈人才得一官，可復開口議禁中事耶！」

translations.literal: He once told his son-in-law Wei Zhiyi to lead the hundred officials in requesting that the Crown Prince supervise the state; Zhiyi immediately said: "Father-in-law, you have only just obtained one office — can you again open your mouth to discuss affairs within the forbidden precincts!"
translations.idiomatic: He once urged his son-in-law Wei Zhiyi to lead the officials in asking the Crown Prince to take charge of government; Wei Zhiyi snapped back, "You have only just won an appointment — must you speak again of palace affairs?"

sentences.zh: 黃裳勃然曰：「黃裳受恩三朝，豈可以一官見買！」

translations.literal: Huangchang flushed with anger and said: "Huangchang has received grace from three reigns — how can he be bought for a single office!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang erupted: "I have served three emperors — you cannot buy my silence with one post!"

sentences.zh: 即拂衣而出。

translations.literal: He immediately brushed his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on his heel and left.

sentences.zh: 尋拜平章事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 邠州節度使韓全義曾居討伐之任，無功，黃裳奏罷之。

translations.literal: Han Quanyi, military commissioner of Binzhou, had once held a punitive campaign assignment without achievement; Huangchang memorialized to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi of Binzhou had led a punitive campaign to no effect; Huangchang had him removed from command.

sentences.zh: 劉辟作亂，議者以劍南險固，不宜生事；

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, those in council said that Jiannan was perilous and secure and that one should not stir up trouble;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rose in rebellion, court opinion held that the rugged Sichuan basin made war inadvisable;

sentences.zh: 唯黃裳堅請討除，憲宗從之。

translations.literal: only Huangchang firmly requested suppression and removal, and Emperor Xianzong followed him.
translations.idiomatic: only Huangchang pressed for a punitive campaign, and Emperor Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 又奏請不以中官為監軍，只委高崇文為使。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting that eunuch officials not be made army supervisors, and that only Gao Chongwen be entrusted as commander.
translations.idiomatic: He further urged that no eunuch supervise the army and that Gao Chongwen alone command the expedition.

sentences.zh: 黃裳自經營伐蜀，以至成功，指授崇文，無不懸合。

translations.literal: From Huangchang's planning of the Shu campaign through to success, every instruction he gave Chongwen hit the mark without exception.
translations.idiomatic: From the planning of the Sichuan campaign through its success, every directive Huangchang gave Gao Chongwen proved exactly right.

sentences.zh: 崇文素憚劉澭，黃裳使人謂崇文曰：「若不奮命，當以劉澭代之。」

translations.literal: Chongwen had always feared Liu Yong; Huangchang sent someone to tell Chongwen: "If you do not exert yourself to the utmost, Liu Yong will be appointed to replace you."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen had long feared rival Liu Yong; Huangchang sent word: "Unless you throw yourself into the fight, Liu Yong will take your place."

sentences.zh: 由是得崇文之死力。

translations.literal: By this means he obtained Chongwen's utmost exertion.
translations.idiomatic: That secured Gao Chongwen's full commitment.

sentences.zh: 既平辟，宰臣入賀，帝目黃裳曰：「此卿之功也。」

translations.literal: After Pi was pacified, the chief ministers entered to offer congratulations; the Emperor looked at Huangchang and said: "This is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi was subdued, the chief ministers came to congratulate the throne; the emperor turned to Huangchang and said, "This victory is yours."

sentences.zh: 後與憲宗語及方鎮除授，黃裳奏曰：「德宗自艱難之後，事多姑息。

translations.literal: Later, speaking with Xianzong about appointments to frontier commands, Huangchang submitted: "Since the hardships, Dezong's affairs were mostly indulgent and accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: Later, discussing frontier appointments with Xianzong, Huangchang said, "After the crises of Dezong's reign, policy grew indulgent toward the regions.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，每帥守物故，必先命中使偵伺其軍動息，其副貳大將中有物望者，必厚賂近臣以求見用，帝必隨其稱美而命之，以是因循，方鎮罕有特命帥守者。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan period, whenever a commander died, the court would first order eunuch envoys to spy on the army's movements; among deputy commanders and great generals with reputation, they would surely bribe close ministers to seek appointment, and the Emperor would follow their praise in appointing them — thus through inertia, frontier commands rarely received specially appointed commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenyuan, whenever a commissioner died, eunuch agents were sent first to gauge the army's mood; deputies with standing bribed court favorites for the post, and the emperor appointed whoever they praised — so that special imperial choices for frontier commands became rare.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜熟思貞元故事，稍以法度整肅諸侯，則天下何憂不治！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should carefully reflect on Zhenyuan precedents and gradually use law and regulation to discipline the regional lords — then what worry is there that the realm will not be well governed!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should study the Zhenyuan precedent and begin disciplining the regional lords by law — then the empire will need no further fear of disorder."

sentences.zh: 憲宗然其言。

translations.literal: Xianzong approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 由是用兵誅蜀、夏之後，不容籓臣蹇傲，克復兩河，威令復振，蓋黃裳啟其衷也。

translations.literal: Thereafter, after employing troops to punish Shu and Xia, he would not tolerate arrogant regional subjects; he recovered the Two He regions, and imperial authority revived — this was essentially Huangchang opening the way.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaigns against Sichuan and Xia, the court would brook no arrogant governors; the Two He were recovered and imperial prestige restored — largely because Huangchang had set the policy in motion.

sentences.zh: 黃裳有經畫之才，達於權變，然檢身律物，寡廉潔之譽，以是居鼎職不久。

translations.literal: Huangchang had talent for planning and strategy and was adept at expedients, yet in regulating himself and disciplining others he had little reputation for integrity; for this reason he did not long hold the highest office.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchang was a gifted strategist skilled at expedients, but he lacked a reputation for personal integrity and therefore did not long remain at the summit of power.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，檢校司空，同平章事，兼河中尹、河中晉絳等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he was made acting Minister of Works, Grand Councillor, and concurrently Governor of Hezhong and military commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, and related prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two he was named acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor, and concurrently took charge of Hezhong as governor and regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八月，封邠國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was created Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，卒於河中，年七十一，贈司徒，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he died at Hezhong, aged seventy-one; posthumously he was made Minister of Education, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Hezhong in the ninth month of year three, at seventy-one; the court posthumously honored him as Minister of Education with the temple name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 黃裳性雅淡寬恕，心雖從長，口不忤物。

translations.literal: Huangchang's nature was refined, mild, and forgiving; though in heart he followed what was right, in speech he did not offend others.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchang was refined and forbearing by nature; he inclined toward the right in private but rarely spoke against anyone in public.

sentences.zh: 始為卿士，女嫁韋執誼，深不為執誼所稱；

translations.literal: When he first became a court noble, his daughter married Wei Zhiyi, yet Zhiyi deeply did not speak well of him;
translations.idiomatic: When he first rose among the nobility, his daughter married Wei Zhiyi, who thought little of him;

sentences.zh: 及執誼譴逐，黃裳終保全之，洎死嶺表，請歸其喪，以辦葬事。

translations.literal: when Zhiyi was condemned and banished, Huangchang ultimately preserved him; when he died in the Lingnan region, Huangchang requested return of his coffin to arrange burial.
translations.idiomatic: when Wei Zhiyi was banished, Huangchang still protected him; after he died in the far south, Huangchang had his remains brought home for burial.

sentences.zh: 及是被疾，醫人誤進其藥，疾甚而不怒。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, a physician mistakenly administered his medicine; his illness grew severe yet he was not angry.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, a doctor gave him the wrong medicine; though his condition worsened, he showed no anger.

sentences.zh: 然為宰相，除授不分流品，或官以賂遷，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Yet as Grand Councillor, in appointments he did not distinguish ranks and grades; some offices were obtained through bribes — contemporary opinion regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, however, he made appointments without regard to rank and sometimes sold offices for bribes, to the regret of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 黃裳歿後，賄賂事發。

translations.literal: After Huangchang's death, the bribery affair came to light.
translations.idiomatic: After Huangchang's death, his bribery scandal surfaced.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，御史臺奏：「前永樂令吳憑為僧鑒虛受托，與故司空杜黃裳，於故州邠寧節度使高崇文處納賂四萬五千貫，並付黃裳男載，按問引伏。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year the Censorate reported: "The former magistrate of Yongle, Wu Ping, acting as agent for the monk Jianxu, together with the late Minister of Works Du Huangchang, accepted at the former Binning military commissioner Gao Chongwen's place a bribe of forty-five thousand strings of cash, all paid to Huangchang's son Zai; on investigation they confessed."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year eight the Censorate reported that former Yongle magistrate Wu Ping, acting for the monk Jianxu, had channeled forty-five thousand strings in bribes from the late Gao Chongwen to Du Huangchang's son Du Zai, and that all parties confessed under interrogation."

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「吳憑曾佐使府，忝履宦途，自宜畏法惜身，豈得為人通貸！

translations.literal: The edict said: "Wu Ping once served in a commissionerate staff and has trod the official path — he should himself fear the law and cherish his person; how could he act as a go-between for others' loans!
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Wu Ping once served on a military staff and ought to have respected the law; how dare he broker illicit payments!

sentences.zh: 事關非道，理合懲愆，宜配流昭州。

translations.literal: The matter touches on improper conduct and rightly calls for punishment; he should be exiled to Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The offense warrants punishment; he is banished to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 其付杜載錢物，宰輔之任，寵寄實深，致茲貨財，不能拒絕，已令按問，悉合征收，貴全終始之恩，俾弘寬大之典。

translations.literal: As for the money and goods paid to Du Zai: the duty of chief minister carried truly deep favor; receiving such wealth, he could not refuse — it has been ordered investigated and all should be levied and collected; yet we value completing the grace from first to last and thereby manifesting the canon of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: The funds paid to Du Zai: as chief minister Du Huangchang had enjoyed exceptional trust; unable to refuse such gifts, he accepted them — all are now to be recovered, yet in honor of his lifelong service the court will show magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 其所取錢物，並宜矜免，杜載等並釋放。」

translations.literal: The money and goods he received should all be treated with compassionate exemption; Du Zai and the others are all to be released."
translations.idiomatic: The sums he took shall be remitted, and Du Zai and the others freed."

sentences.zh: 載為太子仆，長慶中，遷太仆少卿、兼御史中丞，充入吐蕃使。

translations.literal: Zai served as Master of the Crown Prince's Stables; in the Changqing era he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and appointed envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zai served as Master of the Crown Prince's Stables; under Changqing he became Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and Censor-in-Chief and led an embassy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 載弟勝，登進士第，大中朝位給事中。

translations.literal: Zai's younger brother Sheng passed the jinshi examination; in the Dazhong reign he held the post of Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sheng took the jinshi degree and under Dazhong served as Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 勝子廷堅，亦進士擢第。

translations.literal: Sheng's son Tingjian also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's son Tingjian likewise earned the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 高郢

translations.literal: Gao Ye
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye

sentences.zh: 高郢，字公楚，其先渤海蓚人。

translations.literal: Gao Ye, styled Gongchu, his ancestors were from Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye, styled Gongchu, came from a Bohai family originally of Tiao.

sentences.zh: 九歲通《春秋》，能屬文。

translations.literal: At nine he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he had mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and could write essays.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，盜據京邑，父伯祥先為好畤尉，抵賊禁，將加極刑。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, rebels seized the capital; his father Bo Xiang had earlier been magistrate of Haozhi, ran afoul of the rebels' prohibition, and was about to receive extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized the capital at the end of Tianbao, his father Bo Xiang, formerly magistrate of Haozhi, violated rebel law and faced execution.

sentences.zh: 郢時年十五，被髮解衣，請代其父，賊黨義之，乃俱釋。

translations.literal: Ye was then fifteen; he loosened his hair and removed his garments, requesting to replace his father; the rebel band took this as righteous and released them both.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was fifteen; he tore his hair and stripped his upper garment, begging to die in his father's place — moved, the rebels freed them both.

sentences.zh: 後舉進士擢第，應制舉，登茂才異行科，授華陰尉。

translations.literal: Later he passed the jinshi examination, entered the special imperial examination, passed the Maocai Yixing category, and was appointed magistrate of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He later took the jinshi degree, entered the palace examination, passed the category for outstanding talent and conduct, and was made magistrate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 嘗以魯不合用天子禮樂，乃引《公羊傳》，著《魯議》，見稱於時，由是授咸陽尉。

translations.literal: He once held that Lu was unfit to employ the Son of Heaven's ritual and music; he cited the Gongyang Commentary and wrote Discourse on Lu, winning praise in his time — thereby he was appointed magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Arguing that Lu had wrongly assumed royal ritual and music, he cited the Gongyang Commentary in his Discourse on Lu and won contemporary praise, which led to his appointment at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀節制朔方，辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi commanded Shuofang and recruited him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, commanding Shuofang, took him on as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 子儀嘗怒從事張曇，奏殺之；

translations.literal: Ziyi once grew angry at his aide Zhang Tan and memorialized to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi once sought to execute his aide Zhang Tan in anger;

sentences.zh: 郢極言爭救，忤子儀旨，奏貶猗氏丞。

translations.literal: Ye spoke with utmost force to argue and save him, going against Ziyi's intent; he was memorialized for demotion to assistant magistrate of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye pleaded fiercely for Zhang Tan's life, defying Guo Ziyi and earning demotion to assistant magistrate of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 李懷光節制邠寧，奏為從事，累轉副元帥判官、檢校禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang commanded Binning and memorialized to appoint him as aide; he was repeatedly transferred to deputy commander staff judge and Acting Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang of Binning took him as aide; he rose to deputy commander staff judge and acting Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 懷光背叛，將歸河中，郢言：「西迎大駕，豈非忠乎！」

translations.literal: When Huai'guang rebelled and was about to return to Hezhong, Ye said: "To go west and welcome the imperial carriage — is that not loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang rebelled and prepared to withdraw to Hezhong, Ye said, "To march west and welcome the emperor — is that not loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 懷光忿而不聽。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was resentful and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang refused in anger.

sentences.zh: 及歸鎮，又欲悉眾而西。

translations.literal: When he returned to his command, he again wished to lead all his forces west.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his command, he again planned to march west with his full army.

sentences.zh: 時渾瑊軍孤，群帥未集，郢與李鄘誓死駐之。

translations.literal: At that time Hun Jian's army stood isolated and the group of commanders had not yet assembled; Ye and Li Yong pledged to die holding the position.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian's force stood alone while other commanders had not yet gathered; Gao Ye and Li Yong swore to hold the line even unto death.

sentences.zh: 屬懷光長子琟候郢，郢乃諭以逆順曰：「人臣所宜效順。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang's eldest son Wei came to visit Ye, Ye then instructed him on rebellion and obedience, saying: "What a subject should emulate is obedience.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang's eldest son Wei called on him, Gao Ye lectured him on loyalty and rebellion: "A subject's duty is obedience.

sentences.zh: 且自天寶以來阻兵者，今復誰在？

translations.literal: Moreover, of those who have obstructed military authority since Tianbao, who still survives today?
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianbao, which warlord who defied the throne still lives?

sentences.zh: 況國家自有天命，非獨人力。

translations.literal: Moreover the state possesses the Mandate of Heaven of itself — it is not merely human effort.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty holds the Mandate of Heaven by right, not by force alone.

sentences.zh: 今若恃眾西向，自絕於天，十室之邑，必有忠信，安知三軍不有奔潰者乎？」

translations.literal: If now you rely on numbers and turn west, you cut yourself off from Heaven; in a hamlet of ten households there must be loyalty and faith — how do you know the three armies will not have men who flee and collapse?"
translations.idiomatic: If you trust in numbers and march west, you cut yourself off from Heaven; even a village of ten houses holds loyal men — how can you be sure your whole army will not break and run?"

sentences.zh: 李琟震懼，流淚氣索。

translations.literal: Li Wei was shaken with fear, shed tears, and his breath failed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei trembled, wept, and could barely breathe.

sentences.zh: 明年春，郢與都知兵馬使呂鳴嶽、都虞候張延英同謀間道上表；

translations.literal: The next spring, Ye together with the commander of army and horse Lü Mingyue and chief military inspector Zhang Yan'ying jointly plotted to send a memorial by secret route;
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Gao Ye, together with Lü Mingyue and Zhang Yan'ying, smuggled a memorial to the throne;

sentences.zh: 及受密詔，事泄，二將立死。

translations.literal: when they received a secret edict the affair leaked out and the two generals were immediately put to death.
translations.idiomatic: when a secret edict arrived the plot was exposed and both generals were executed at once.

sentences.zh: 懷光乃大集將卒，白刃盈庭，引郢詰之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang then greatly assembled officers and soldiers, naked blades filling the courtyard, and brought Ye forward to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang mustered his officers with blades drawn across the courtyard and summoned Gao Ye for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 郢挺然抗辭，無所慚隱，憤氣感發，觀者淚下，懷光慚沮而止。

translations.literal: Ye stood upright with defiant words, without shame or concealment; indignant spirit moved those present to tears; Huai'guang, ashamed and dejected, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye answered uprightly without evasion; his righteous anger moved onlookers to tears, and Huai'guang, abashed, desisted.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，命諫議大夫孔巢父、中人啖守盈赴河中宣慰懷光，授以太保；

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital, he ordered Remonstrance Official Kong Chaofu and the eunuch Tan Shouying to go to Hezhong to console and reassure Huai'guang, appointing him Grand Mentor;
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to Chang'an, he sent Kong Chaofu and the eunuch Tan Shouying to Hezhong to reassure Huai'guang and named him Grand Mentor;

sentences.zh: 而懷光怒，激其親兵詬詈，殺守盈及巢父。

translations.literal: but Huai'guang grew angry, stirred his personal troops to revile them, and killed Shouying and Chaofu.
translations.idiomatic: but Huai'guang roused his guards to abuse them and had both men killed.

sentences.zh: 巢父之被刃也，委於地，郢就而撫之。

translations.literal: When Chaofu was cut down, he was cast upon the ground; Ye went to him and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Chaofu fell, Gao Ye went to his body and tended him.

sentences.zh: 乃懷光被誅，馬燧辟郢為掌書記。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Huai'guang was executed, Ma Sui recruited Ye as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'guang was put to death, Ma Sui took Gao Ye as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征拜主客員外，遷刑部郎中，改中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Office for Guests of the Dependencies; promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice; changed to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was called to court as Vice Director of Foreign Guests, then Director in the Ministry of Justice, and finally Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 凡九歲，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In all, nine years passed, and he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時應進士舉者，多務朋遊，馳逐聲名；

translations.literal: At that time those taking the jinshi examination mostly pursued factional socializing and raced after reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Candidates for the jinshi degree then spent their time in cliques and chasing fame;

sentences.zh: 每歲冬，州府薦送後，唯追奉宴集，罕肄其業。

translations.literal: every winter, after prefectural recommendation and forwarding, they only pursued banquets and gatherings, rarely cultivating their studies.
translations.idiomatic: each winter, after provincial nomination, they attended feasts rather than studying.

sentences.zh: 郢性剛正，尤嫉其風，既領職，拒絕請托，雖同列通熟，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was upright and firm; he especially detested this custom; once he took office he refused requests and entreaties — even colleagues who were on familiar terms did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye was stern and upright and detested the custom; once in office he refused all solicitations, and even close colleagues dared not intercede.

sentences.zh: 誌在經藝，專考程試。

translations.literal: His aim lay in the classics and arts; he devoted himself to examining according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He focused on the classics and examined candidates strictly by the rules.

sentences.zh: 凡掌貢部三歲，進幽獨，抑浮華，朋濫之風，翕然一變。

translations.literal: In all he directed the tribute department for three years, advancing the secluded and solitary, suppressing the flashy and ornate — the wind of factional excess suddenly changed as one.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years heading the examinations he promoted serious scholars, curbed display, and the clique culture changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 拜太常卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年冬，進位銀青光祿大夫，守中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he advanced to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Zhenyuan nineteen he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master and made acting Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，轉刑部尚書，為韋執誼等所憚。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Minister of Justice; Wei Zhiyi and others feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, he became Minister of Justice, whom Wei Zhiyi and his faction feared.

sentences.zh: 尋罷知政事，以本官判吏部尚書事。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed from managing state affairs and with his existing office adjudicated the affairs of the Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon removed from the council and assigned to oversee the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年，出鎮華州。

translations.literal: The next year he went out to command Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent to govern Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 元和元年冬，復拜太常卿，尋除御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yuanhe he was again appointed Director of Ritual; soon he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yuanhe one he returned as Director of Ritual and soon became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 數月，轉兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Several months later he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 逾月，再表乞骸，不許。

translations.literal: After more than a month he again memorialized begging to retire on account of his bones; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he memorialized again to retire; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 又上言曰：「臣聞勞生佚老，天理自然，蠕動翾飛，日入皆息。

translations.literal: He again submitted saying: "Your servant has heard that to labor in life and rest in old age is Heaven's principle and nature's way; wriggling creatures and flying things all cease at sunset.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again: "I have heard that to toil in youth and rest in age is nature's law; crawling things and flying birds all cease at sunset.

sentences.zh: 自非貢禹之守經據古，趙喜之正身匪懈，韓暨之誌節高潔，山濤之道德模表，縱過常期，詎為貪冒。

translations.literal: Unless one is like Gong Yu in holding to the classics and grounding in antiquity, Zhao Xi in rectifying the person without slackness, Han Ji in lofty integrity and purity of aim, or Shan Tao in moral virtue as a model — even if one passes the usual term, how could it be greed and presumption?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one were Gong Yu clinging to the classics, Zhao Xi upright without slackness, Han Ji of lofty integrity, or Shan Tao a moral exemplar, to linger past one's term would be mere greed.

sentences.zh: 其有當仁不讓，急病忘身，豈止君命，猶宜身舉。

translations.literal: When there is duty to humanity one should not yield; when illness is urgent one forgets the person — this is not only the ruler's command but still fitting that one offer oneself.
translations.idiomatic: When duty calls one should not refuse; in urgent need one forgets self — that is not only the sovereign's command but what one should volunteer for oneself.

sentences.zh: 臣郢不才，久辱高位，無任由衷瀝懇之至。」

translations.literal: Your servant Ye lacks talent and has long suffered the disgrace of a high position; there is no reason not to pour out the utmost sincerity from the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Ye is without talent and has long occupied high office undeservedly; I have no excuse not to speak my heart plainly."

sentences.zh: 乃授尚書右僕射致仕。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted retirement as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年七月卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of year six, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the temple name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 郢性恭慎廉潔，罕與人交遊，守官奉法勤恪，掌誥累年，家無制草。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was respectful, cautious, incorrupt, and clean; he rarely socialized with others; in holding office he observed law with diligence; for many years he managed edicts, yet his household had no drafts of proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye was respectful, cautious, and incorruptible, rarely socializing; diligent in office, he drafted edicts for years yet kept no copies at home.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「前輩皆留制集，公焚之何也？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "Former generations all kept collections of proclamations — why do you burn yours?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "Earlier drafters all kept collections of edicts — why do you burn yours?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「王言不可存私家。」

translations.literal: He said: "The king's words must not be stored in a private household."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Imperial words must not be kept in private homes."

sentences.zh: 時人重其慎密。

translations.literal: People of the time valued his discretion and secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired his discretion.

sentences.zh: 與鄭珣瑜並命拜相；

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councillor on the same order as Zheng Xunyu;
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the council on the same edict as Zheng Xunyu;

sentences.zh: 未幾，德宗升遐。

translations.literal: Before long, Dezong ascended to the distant realm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Emperor Dezong died.

sentences.zh: 時同在相位，杜佑以宿舊居上，而韋執誼由朋黨專柄。

translations.literal: At that time they were together in the council; Du You, by virtue of long standing, ranked above, while Wei Zhiyi through faction held sole power.
translations.idiomatic: They served together on the council; Du You, as the senior figure, took precedence, while Wei Zhiyi monopolized power through his faction.

sentences.zh: 順宗風恙方甚，樞機不宣，而王叔文以翰林學士兼戶部侍郎，充度支副使。

translations.literal: Shunzong's wind ailment was then severe and the pivots of state were not proclaimed; meanwhile Wang Shuwen, as Hanlin Academician and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, served as deputy commissioner of the Department of Public Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shunzong was gravely ill and did not handle affairs, while Wang Shuwen, as Hanlin scholar and Vice Minister of Revenue, served as deputy fiscal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時政事，王叔文謀議，王伾通導，李忠言宣下，韋執誼奉行。

translations.literal: At that time in state affairs: Wang Shuwen plotted and deliberated, Wang Pi conveyed and guided, Li Zhongyan proclaimed downward, and Wei Zhiyi carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Government then ran through Wang Shuwen's planning, Wang Pi's coordination, Li Zhongyan's pronouncements, and Wei Zhiyi's execution.

sentences.zh: 珣瑜自受命，憂形顏色，至是以勢不可奪，因稱疾不起。

translations.literal: From the time Xunyu received his appointment, worry showed on his countenance; by now, seeing the power could not be wrested away, he therefore claimed illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xunyu had looked troubled from the day he took office; now, seeing power beyond recovery, he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 郢則因循，竟無所發，以至於罷。

translations.literal: Ye, by contrast, followed inertia, ultimately accomplishing nothing, until he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye drifted along, achieved nothing, and was eventually dismissed.

sentences.zh: 物論定此為優劣焉。

translations.literal: Public opinion fixed this as the measure of superiority and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion judged which conduct was superior.

sentences.zh: 子定嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ding succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding carried on the line.

sentences.zh: 定，幼聰警絕倫，年七歲時，讀《尚書•湯誓》，問郢曰：「奈何以臣伐君？」

translations.literal: Ding in youth was brilliantly perceptive beyond his peers; at seven, reading the Tang Oath in the Documents, he asked Ye: "How can a subject attack his lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Ding was extraordinarily precocious; at seven, reading the Tang Oath in the Documents, he asked his father, "How can a subject attack his ruler?"

sentences.zh: 郢曰：「應天順人，不為非道。」

translations.literal: Ye said: "To respond to Heaven and accord with the people is not an improper way."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ye answered, "To follow Heaven and win the people is not wrongdoing."

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「用命賞於祖，不用命戮於社，是順人乎？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "Those who obey receive reward at the ancestral temple; those who disobey are executed at the altar of the land—is this according with the people?"
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on: "The oath rewards obedience at the ancestral shrine and punishes defiance at the land altar—how does that win the people?"

sentences.zh: 父不能對。

translations.literal: His father could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: His father had no answer.

sentences.zh: 仕至京兆參軍。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Administrative Assistant of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer under the metropolitan magistrate of the capital.

sentences.zh: 小字董二，人以幼慧，多以字稱之。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Dong the Second; because people admired his youthful brilliance, they often addressed him by this name.
translations.idiomatic: Known from childhood as Dong Er, he was so famed for precocity that people commonly called him by that nickname.

sentences.zh: 尤精《王氏易》，嘗為《易圖》，合入出以畫八卦，上圓下方，合則重，轉則演，七轉而六十四卦六甲八節備焉。

translations.literal: He was especially adept in "Mr. Wang's Changes"; once he made a "Diagram of the Changes," combining entry and exit to draw the Eight Trigrams—round above and square below; when joined they doubled, when turned they unfolded; with seven turns the sixty-four hexagrams, the six jia, and the eight seasonal nodes were all complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Wang Bi's "Book of Changes" and devised an "Diagram of the Changes" that mapped the Eight Trigrams from cosmic ingress and egress—round heaven above, square earth below, layers that multiplied when stacked and permutations that unfolded when rotated—so that seven revolutions yielded all sixty-four hexagrams together with the cycles of the six jia and the eight seasonal divisions.

sentences.zh: 著《易外傳》二十二卷。

translations.literal: He authored "Supplementary Transmission of the Changes" in twenty-two juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the "Supplementary Transmission of the Changes" in twenty-two volumes.

sentences.zh: 杜佑

translations.literal: Du You
translations.idiomatic: Du You

sentences.zh: 杜佑，字君卿，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Du You, styled Junqing, was a native of Wannian in the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du You (Junqing) came from Wannian County in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 曾祖行敏，荊、益二州都督府長史、南陽郡公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xingmin served as chief administrator of the Jing and Yi area commandants' offices and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Du Xingmin was chief administrator under the Jing and Yi military governors and held the title Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖愨，右司員外郎、詳正學士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Que served as vice director in the Right Bureau and as examining academician of detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Du Que was a vice director in the Ministry of Justice and an examiner in the Office of Detailed Review.

sentences.zh: 父希望，歷鴻臚卿、恆州刺史、西河太守，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: His father Xiwang successively served as Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, Governor of Hengzhou, and Prefect of Xihe, and was posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Xiwang had been director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, governor of Hengzhou, and prefect of Xihe, and was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 佑以廕入仕，補濟南郡參軍、剡縣丞。

translations.literal: You entered office through yin privilege, and was appointed Staff Officer of Ji'nan Commandery and Assistant Magistrate of Shan County.
translations.idiomatic: Du You entered government by hereditary privilege, first as staff officer for Ji'nan commandery and then as assistant magistrate of Shan county.

sentences.zh: 時潤州刺史韋元甫嘗受恩於希望，佑謁見，元甫未之知，以故人子待之。

translations.literal: At that time Runzhou Prefect Wei Yuanfu had once received favor from Xiwang; You called on him, but Yuanfu did not recognize him and treated him as the son of an old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhou prefect Wei Yuanfu had once been indebted to Du Xiwang; when Du You paid his respects, Yuanfu did not recognize him and treated him merely as an old friend's son.

sentences.zh: 他日，元甫視事，有疑獄不能決。

translations.literal: Another day Yuanfu held court; there was a doubtful criminal case he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, while Yuanfu was holding court, he could not resolve a doubtful criminal case.

sentences.zh: 佑時在旁，元甫試訊於佑；

translations.literal: You was then at his side; Yuanfu tried questioning You;
translations.idiomatic: Du You happened to be nearby, and Yuanfu tried questioning him;

sentences.zh: 佑口對響應，皆得其要。

translations.literal: You answered orally in resonant response, all grasping the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Du You answered fluently and hit every essential point.

sentences.zh: 元甫奇之，乃奏為司法參軍。

translations.literal: Yuanfu marveled at him and thereupon memorialized to appoint him Judicial Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was impressed and recommended him for appointment as judicial aide.

sentences.zh: 元甫為浙西觀察、淮南節度，皆辟為從事，深所委信。

translations.literal: When Yuanfu served as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhexi and Military Commissioner of Huainan, he recruited You as staff member both times and relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuanfu served as Zhexi surveillance commissioner or Huainan military commissioner, he recruited Du You as a staff officer and trusted him completely.

sentences.zh: 累官至檢校主客員外郎，入為工部郎中，充江西青苗使，轉撫州刺史。

translations.literal: By accumulated promotion he reached Acting Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions, entered as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works, served as Green-Grain Commissioner for Jiangxi, and was transferred to Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to acting vice director of the Bureau of Receptions, entered the capital as bureau director in the Ministry of Works, served as green-grain commissioner for Jiangxi, and was transferred to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 改御史中丞，充容管經略使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief and commissioned as Military Commissioner of Rongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and appointed military commissioner of Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 楊炎入相，征入朝，歷工部、金部二郎中，並充水陸轉運使，改度支郎中，兼和糴等使。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan entered the council, You was summoned to court, successively serving as bureau director in the Ministries of Works and Revenue, concurrently as Commissioner for Water and Land Transport, then changed to Bureau Director of the Department of Revenue and concurrently Commissioner for Equitable Purchase and related duties.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yan became chief minister, Du You was recalled to the capital, served successively as bureau director in the Ministries of Works and Revenue, headed water and land transport, then became director of the revenue bureau while also overseeing equitable purchase and related fiscal offices.

sentences.zh: 時方軍興，饋運之務，悉委於佑；

translations.literal: At that time warfare had just arisen, and the affairs of supply transport were entirely entrusted to You;
translations.idiomatic: With war just underway, all supply and transport duties were placed in his hands;

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Director of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of revenue and put in charge of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 為盧杞所惡，出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: Detested by Lu Qi, he was sent out as Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi turned against him and had him posted out as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 佑母在，杞以蘇州憂闕授之。

translations.literal: You's mother was still living; Qi assigned him Suzhou knowing mourning duties awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Du You's mother was still alive; Qi gave him Suzhou precisely because the post would soon fall vacant for mourning.

sentences.zh: 佑不行，俄換饒州刺史。

translations.literal: You did not go; shortly he was changed to Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du You refused to take up the post and was soon reassigned as prefect of Raozhou instead.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼御史大夫，充嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was given concurrent title of Chief Censor and commissioned as Military Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made chief censor and military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 時德宗在興元。

translations.literal: At that time Dezong was at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷故事，執政往往遺脫；

translations.literal: By court precedent, those at the helm often omitted details;
translations.idiomatic: Court routine often let those in charge skip formalities;

sentences.zh: 舊嶺南節度，常兼五管經略使，佑獨不兼。

translations.literal: Under the old arrangement the Lingnan military commissioner usually also held the post of Five-Circuits Military Commissioner; You alone was not given the concurrent title.
translations.idiomatic: Traditionally the Lingnan commissioner also oversaw the five frontier circuits, but Du You alone was not given that concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 故五管不屬嶺南，自佑始也。

translations.literal: Hence the five circuits did not fall under Lingnan's jurisdiction—from You this began.
translations.idiomatic: From his appointment onward the five circuits were no longer subordinate to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，徵為尚書左丞，又出為陜州觀察使，遷檢校禮部尚書、揚州大都督府長史，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanzhou, and promoted to Acting Minister of Rites and Chief Administrator of Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, commissioned as Huainan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 787 he was recalled as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, then posted as Shaanzhou surveillance commissioner, and soon promoted to acting minister of rites and chief administrator of Yangzhou while serving as Huainan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，特詔起復，累轉刑部尚書、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, by special edict he was called back to service and successively promoted to Minister of Justice and Acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning by special edict and rose to minister of justice and acting right vice director.

sentences.zh: 十六年，徐州節度使張建封卒，其子愔為三軍所立，詔佑以淮南節制檢校左僕射、同平章事，兼徐泗節度使，委以討伐。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Zhang Jianfeng, Military Commissioner of Xuzhou, died; his son Yin was installed by the three armies. An edict appointed You, under Huainan regulation, as Acting Left Vice Director and Councilor, concurrently Military Commissioner of Xu-Si, with responsibility for the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In 800 Zhang Jianfeng, commissioner of Xuzhou, died and the army installed his son Zhang Yin; Du You was ordered, under Huainan authority, to become acting left vice director and councilor while also commanding Xu-Si and leading the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 佑乃大具舟艦，遣將孟準先當之。

translations.literal: You then greatly prepared warships and dispatched the general Meng Zhun to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Du You massed a large fleet and sent General Meng Zhun ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 準渡淮而敗，佑杖之，固境不敢進。

translations.literal: Zhun crossed the Huai and was defeated; You had him beaten with the rod, and the army held the border without daring advance.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhun crossed the Huai and was defeated; Du You had him flogged, and the force held its positions without pressing forward.

sentences.zh: 及詔以徐州授愔，而加佑兼濠、泗等州觀察使。

translations.literal: When an edict granted Xuzhou to Yin and added for You concurrent oversight of Hao, Si, and other prefectures as Surveillance Commissioner,
translations.idiomatic: When an edict recognized Zhang Yin's control of Xuzhou and added Hao, Si, and neighboring prefectures to Du You's surveillance portfolio,

sentences.zh: 在揚州開設營壘三十餘所，士馬修葺。

translations.literal: at Yangzhou he established more than thirty fortified camps; troops and horses were repaired and maintained.
translations.idiomatic: he built more than thirty fortified camps around Yangzhou and kept troops and horses in good repair.

sentences.zh: 然於賓僚間依阿無制，判官南宮僔、李亞、鄭元均爭權，頗紊軍政，德宗知之，並竄於嶺外。

translations.literal: Yet among retainers and staff he was irresolute and without restraint; judicial aides Nangong Pu, Li Ya, and Zheng Yuanjun struggled for power and greatly disordered military administration. Dezong knew of it and exiled them all beyond the Lingnan passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was indecisive with his staff, and judicial aides Nangong Pu, Li Ya, and Zheng Yuanjun fought for power and badly disrupted military affairs; when Dezong learned of it he exiled all three beyond the Lingnan frontier.

sentences.zh: 十九年入朝，拜檢校司空、同平章事，充太清宮使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he entered court and was appointed Acting Minister of Works, Councilor, and Commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 803 he came to court and was made acting minister of works, councilor, and commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，佑攝冢宰，尋進位檢校司徒，充度支鹽鐵等使，依前平章事。

translations.literal: When Dezong died, You acted as chief funeral director; soon he was advanced to Acting Minister of Works and commissioned for the Department of Revenue, Salt Iron, and related offices, continuing as before as Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong died, Du You served as chief funeral director; he was soon promoted to acting minister of works, put in charge of revenue, salt iron, and related fiscal offices, and continued as councilor.

sentences.zh: 旋又加弘文館大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was also made Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made grand academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文為副使，佑雖總統，而權歸叔文。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shuwen was deputy commissioner; although You was overall chief, power rested with Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen was then deputy commissioner; though Du You nominally headed the office, real power lay with Wang Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 叔文敗，又奏李巽為副使，頗有所立。

translations.literal: When Shuwen fell, You again memorialized Li Xun as deputy commissioner and achieved quite a few reforms.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shuwen's fall he recommended Li Xun as deputy and carried out several useful reforms.

sentences.zh: 順宗崩，佑復攝冢宰，尋讓金谷之務，引李巽自代。

translations.literal: When Shunzong died, You again acted as chief funeral director; soon he relinquished fiscal matters and brought in Li Xun to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong died he again directed the funeral rites, then soon handed fiscal affairs to Li Xun and stepped aside.

sentences.zh: 先是，度支以制用惜費，漸權百司之職，廣署吏員，繁而難理；

translations.literal: Previously, the Department of Revenue, in economizing expenditures, had gradually taken over duties of the hundred offices, broadly appointing staff until administration was cumbersome and hard to govern;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the revenue bureau, trying to cut costs, had gradually absorbed duties from other agencies, swelling its staff until the bureaucracy became unwieldy;

sentences.zh: 佑始奏營繕歸之將作，木炭歸之司農，染練歸之少府，綱條頗整，公議多之，朝廷允其議。

translations.literal: You first memorialized that construction and repair return to the Directorate of Imperial Works, charcoal to the Directorate of Imperial Granaries, dyeing and finishing to the Court of the Imperial Treasury; the regulations became rather well ordered. Public discussion praised this widely, and the court approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Du You first proposed returning construction to the Directorate of Imperial Works, charcoal to the Directorate of Imperial Granaries, and dyeing to the Court of the Imperial Treasury; the lines of authority became much clearer, public opinion strongly favored the change, and the court approved it.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，冊拜司徒、同平章事，封岐國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was enfeoffed at court as Minister of Works, Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In 806 he was formally invested as minister of works and councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 時河西党項潛導吐蕃入寇，邊將邀功，亟請擊之。

translations.literal: At that time in the Hexi region the Tangut secretly guided the Tibetans to raid in; border generals sought merit and repeatedly asked to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut tribes in the Hexi corridor were secretly guiding Tibetan raids, and frontier generals eager for glory kept urging attacks.

sentences.zh: 佑上疏論之曰：

translations.literal: You submitted a memorial arguing against it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Du You submitted a memorial arguing against this, writing:

sentences.zh: 臣伏見党項與西戎潛通，屢有降人指陳事跡，而公卿廷議，以為誠當謹兵戎，備侵軼，益發甲卒，邀其寇暴。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that the Tangut and the western barbarians communicate in secret; repeatedly surrendering men have pointed out matters in detail, yet in court deliberation the grandees hold that one truly ought to strengthen military preparedness, guard against incursions, and further send out armored soldiers to intercept their raids.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that the Tangut are in secret contact with western tribes, and deserters have repeatedly reported the facts, yet the ministers in court argue that we must tighten defenses, guard against raids, and send more armored troops to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 此蓋未達事機，匹夫之常論也。

translations.literal: This probably fails to grasp the circumstances of affairs—it is the ordinary opinion of the common man.
translations.idiomatic: That view fails to grasp the real situation—it is the reflex of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 夫蠻夷猾夏，唐虞已然。

translations.literal: Barbarians troubling China was already so in the time of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian trouble for China dates back even to Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 周宣中興，獫狁為害，但命南仲往城朔方，追之太原，及境而止，誠不欲弊中國而怒遠夷也。

translations.literal: At the restoration of King Xuan of Zhou, the Xianyun did harm; he only ordered Nan Zhong to go and fortify Shuofang, pursued them to Taiyuan, and stopped at the border—truly not wishing to exhaust China and enrage distant tribes.
translations.idiomatic: At King Xuan's restoration the Xianyun were a menace, yet he only sent Nan Zhong to fortify Shuofang, pursued them to Taiyuan, and stopped at the border—he did not wish to exhaust the realm and provoke distant tribes.

sentences.zh: 秦平六國，恃其兵力，北築長城，以拒匈奴；

translations.literal: Qin after pacifying the Six States relied on its military strength, built the Long Wall northward to repel the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: After Qin unified the six states it relied on force, built the Long Wall to the north against the Xiongnu,

sentences.zh: 西逐諸羌，出於塞外。

translations.literal: westward they drove the various Qiang beyond the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: and drove the Qiang west beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 勞力擾人，結怨階亂，中國未靜，白徒競起，海內雲擾，實生謫戍。

translations.literal: Labor exhausted the people and stirred resentment, hate accumulated and disorder arose; China was not yet tranquil when bare-hands bands swarmed up and the realm was clouded with disturbance—this in truth produced the exiles on frontier guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: The labor burdened the people, bred resentment, and led to chaos; the interior was not yet settled when unarmed mobs rose everywhere and the realm fell into turmoil—the very source of the conscript frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 漢武因文、景之富，命將興師，遂至戶口減半，竟下哀痛之詔罷田輪臺。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, relying on the wealth of Wen and Jing, ordered generals to raise armies, until household registers were halved; he finally issued the edict of anguish abolishing the fields at Lun Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, drawing on the prosperity of Wen and Jing, launched campaigns until the population was halved, and finally issued his repentant edict abandoning the fields at Lun Terrace.

sentences.zh: 前史書之，尚嘉其先迷而後復。

translations.literal: The former histories record it and still commend one who first lost the way and afterward returned.
translations.idiomatic: The histories still praise him for erring first and correcting himself afterward.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖王之理天下也，唯務綏靜蒸人，西至流沙，東漸於海，在南與北，亦存聲教。

translations.literal: For the sage king in ordering all under Heaven, he solely attends to pacifying and quieting the multitudes; west to the shifting sands, east reaching the sea, south and north alike, he preserves civilizing instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The sage ruler governs the realm by calming the people—west to the shifting sands, east to the sea, north and south alike—through civilizing influence rather than force.

sentences.zh: 不以遠物為珍，匪求遐方之貢，豈疲內而事外，終得少而失多。

translations.literal: He does not take distant things as treasures nor seek tribute from remote regions—how could he weary the interior to serve the exterior, and in the end gain little while losing much?
translations.idiomatic: He does not prize exotic goods or demand distant tribute; why exhaust the interior for the frontier and end with more loss than gain?

sentences.zh: 故前代納忠之臣，並有匡君之議。

translations.literal: Hence loyal ministers of former ages all had proposals to correct their lords.
translations.idiomatic: That is why loyal ministers of past dynasties all offered counsel to steer their rulers right.

sentences.zh: 淮南王請息師於閩越，賈捐之願棄地於珠崖，安危利害，高懸前史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huainan asked to cease troops against Minyue; Jia Juanzhi wished to abandon territory at Zhuya—the safety and danger, benefit and harm, hang high in former histories.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huainan urged halting war against Minyue; Jia Juanzhi argued for abandoning Zhuya—the lessons of safety and danger stand clear in the histories.

sentences.zh: 昔馮奉世矯漢帝之詔，擊莎車，傳其王首於京師，威震西域。

translations.literal: Formerly Feng Fengshi, feigning the Han Emperor's edict, attacked Shache and sent the king's head to the capital—awe shaking the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Feng Fengshi forged an imperial order, attacked Shache, and sent the king's head to the capital, his fame shaking the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 宣帝大悅，議加爵土之賞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan was greatly pleased and discussed adding reward of noble rank and territory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was delighted and considered granting him rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 蕭望之獨以為矯制違命，雖有功效，不可為法；

translations.literal: Xiao Wangzhi alone held that feigning edict and violating command, though there were achievements, could not serve as precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Wangzhi alone argued that forging orders and defying command, however successful, must not become precedent;

sentences.zh: 恐後之奉使者爭逐發兵，為國家生事，述理明白，其言遂行。

translations.literal: he feared that later envoys would compete to dispatch troops and create affairs for the state; his reasoning was clear and his words were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: lest future envoys compete to raise troops and create trouble for the state; his reasoning was clear and his view prevailed.

sentences.zh: 國家自天後已來，突厥默啜兵強氣勇，屢寇邊城，為害頗甚。

translations.literal: Since the Empress Wu the state had seen the Turk Mohe chaghan strong in troops and bold in spirit, repeatedly raiding border cities with considerable harm.
translations.idiomatic: Since Empress Wu's reign the Turk qaghan Mo-chuo had been strong and bold, raiding the frontier repeatedly with great damage.

sentences.zh: 開元初，邊將郝靈佺親捕斬之，傳首闕下，自以為功，代莫與二，坐望榮寵。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan period the border general Hao Lingqian personally captured and beheaded him, sent the head below the gates; he considered himself without peer in merit for a generation and sat expecting honor and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan the frontier general Hao Lingqian captured and killed him and sent the head to the capital; he thought his achievement unmatched and waited for lavish reward.

sentences.zh: 宋璟為相，慮武臣邀功，為國生事，止授以郎將。

translations.literal: Song Jing as chancellor, fearing military men seeking merit would create affairs for the state, only appointed him a commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Song Jing, fearing that rewarding martial ambition would stir trouble, gave him only a commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 由是訖開元之盛，無人復議開邊，中國遂寧，外夷亦靜。

translations.literal: From this until the greatness of Kaiyuan, no one again debated opening the frontier; China thereby grew tranquil and outer tribes also grew quiet.
translations.idiomatic: From then through Kaiyuan's golden age no one again urged frontier campaigns; the interior grew peaceful and the outer tribes calm.

sentences.zh: 此皆成敗可徵，鑒戒非遠。

translations.literal: These are all success and failure that can be verified—warnings not far off.
translations.idiomatic: These are lessons of success and failure close at hand, not distant warnings.

sentences.zh: 且党項小蕃，雜處中國，本懷我德，當示撫綏。

translations.literal: Moreover the Tangut are a small tribe scattered within China; they originally embrace our virtue and ought to be shown soothing governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut are a small people living among us; they once embraced our virtue and should be shown gentle rule.

sentences.zh: 間者邊將非廉，亟有侵刻，或利其善馬，或取其子女，便賄方物，徵發役徒。

translations.literal: Recently border generals have not been upright and have repeatedly encroached—sometimes profiting from their fine horses, sometimes taking their sons and daughters, demanding regional products, conscripting laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Lately frontier officers have been corrupt, repeatedly extorting them—seizing fine horses, taking sons and daughters, demanding local goods, and conscripting labor.

sentences.zh: 勞苦既多，叛亡遂起，或與北狄通使，或與西戎寇邊，有為使然，固當懲革。

translations.literal: When toil and hardship grew many, defection and flight then arose; some communicated with the northern Di, some with the western Rong raided the border—when causes produce this, it is right to punish and reform.
translations.idiomatic: As hardship mounted, flight and rebellion followed; some deal with northern tribes, others guide western raiders—where causes exist, reform is surely needed.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「遠人不服，則修文德以來之。」

translations.literal: The "Commentary" says: "When distant men do not submit, then cultivate civil virtue to bring them in."
translations.idiomatic: The "Commentary" says: "When distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to win them."

sentences.zh: 《管子》曰：「國家無使勇猛者為邊境。」

translations.literal: The "Guanzi" says: "Let not the state place fierce fighters on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: The "Guanzi" says: "Do not station fierce men on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 此誠聖哲識微知著之遠略也。

translations.literal: This is truly the far-sighted strategy of a sage who perceives the subtle and knows what will appear.
translations.idiomatic: That is the far-sighted policy of sages who see the small sign and grasp what follows.

sentences.zh: 今戎醜方強，邊備未實，誠宜慎擇良將，誡之完葺，使保誠信，絕其求取，用示懷柔。

translations.literal: Now the Rong rebels are just strong and border defenses are not yet solid; one truly ought carefully to select good generals, admonish them to complete repairs, cause them to preserve faith and sincerity, cut off their demands and takings, and use this to show gentle appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: The Rong are strong and frontier defenses weak; we should choose good commanders, order them to repair defenses, keep faith, stop extortion, and show forbearance.

sentences.zh: 來則懲禦，去則謹備，自然懷柔，革其奸謀，何必遽圖興師，坐致勞費！

translations.literal: When they come, then punish and repel; when they go, then guard carefully—in natural fashion they will submit, their treacherous plots will be reformed; why urgently plot to raise troops and by sitting achieve labor and expense!
translations.idiomatic: Punish them when they come, guard when they leave, and they will submit of themselves and abandon intrigue—why rush to war and waste treasure idle?

sentences.zh: 陛下上聖君人，覆育群類，動必師古，謀無不臧。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is a supreme sage ruler over men, sheltering and nurturing the multitudes; in movement you always take antiquity as teacher, in counsel none is not good.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a sage sovereign who nurtures all beings, takes antiquity as your guide in every act, and whose plans are always sound.

sentences.zh: 伏望堅保永圖，置兵衽席，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will firmly preserve the eternal plan, set weapons on the mat and seat—all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to hold fast to this long-term design and keep arms folded on the mat—the realm would be greatly blessed!

sentences.zh: 臣識昧經綸，學慚博究，竊鼎鉉之寵任，為朝廷之老臣，恩深莫倫，誌懇思報，臧否備閱，芻蕘上陳，有瀆旒扆，伏深惶悚。

translations.literal: Your subject's knowledge is dim in statecraft, my learning ashamed before broad inquiry; I usurp the favored trust of the tripod cauldron, serve the court as an old minister—grace deep beyond compare, my will earnest to think on repayment; good and bad all reviewed, firewood and hay offered upward—I have offended the imperial screen and prostrate myself in deep dread.
translations.idiomatic: My grasp of statecraft is shallow and my learning meager, yet I hold the highest trust and am an old minister of the court; your grace is beyond measure and my will is bent on repayment. Having weighed right and wrong I offer this humble counsel; if I have offended the throne I prostrate myself in deepest fear.

sentences.zh: 上深嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，請致仕，詔不許，但令三五日一入中書，平章政事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he requested retirement; the edict did not permit it but only ordered him to enter the Central Secretariat every three or five days to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he asked to retire; the throne refused but allowed him to attend the Secretariat every few days to deliberate on policy.

sentences.zh: 每入奏事，憲宗優禮之；

translations.literal: Each time he entered to memorialize affairs, Xianzong treated him with exceptional courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to report, Xianzong treated him with special courtesy;

sentences.zh: 不名，常呼司徒。

translations.literal: he was not called by name but was always addressed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: he was never called by name but always addressed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 佑城南樊川有佳林亭，卉木幽邃，佑每與公卿宴集其間，廣陳妓樂。

translations.literal: You had a fine grove pavilion at Fancy Woods in Fanchuan south of the city—plants and trees deeply secluded; You often held banquets there with grandees, lavishly displaying courtesans and music.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city at Fanchuan Du You had a fine grove pavilion amid deep-shaded trees; he often entertained grandees there with music and dancers.

sentences.zh: 諸子咸居朝列，當時貴盛，莫之與比。

translations.literal: All his sons held posts in the court ranks; at the time their eminence had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons held court office; at the time no family matched their eminence.

sentences.zh: 元和七年，被疾，六月，復乞骸骨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe he fell ill; in the sixth month he again begged to return his bones.
translations.idiomatic: In 812 he fell ill and in the sixth month again petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 表四上，情理切至，憲宗不獲已，許之。

translations.literal: He submitted four memorials; reasoning and feeling were pressing to the utmost; Xianzong had no choice, and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted four petitions of such force and pathos that Xianzong could refuse no longer and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict read:

sentences.zh: 宣力濟時，為臣之懿躅；

translations.literal: To display strength and aid the age is the excellent pace of a minister;
translations.idiomatic: To exert one's strength for the age is the finest duty of a minister;

sentences.zh: 辭榮告老，行己之高風。

translations.literal: To decline glory and announce old age is the lofty wind of one's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: To decline honor and announce one's retirement is the noblest conduct.

sentences.zh: 況乎任重公臺，義深翼贊，秉沖讓之誌，堅金石之誠。

translations.literal: Moreover, bearing the weight of the Three Excellencies, righteousness deep in wing-assistance, holding the will of humble yielding, firm as metal and stone in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you have borne the weight of the highest offices, your righteousness has deeply aided the throne, you hold to modesty, and your sincerity is firm as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 敦諭既勤，所執彌固，則當遂其衷懇，進以崇名；

translations.literal: Since earnest exhortation has been diligent and what is held grows firmer, then one ought to follow his heartfelt plea and advance him with exalted title;
translations.idiomatic: Since repeated entreaties have failed and your resolve grows firmer, we shall grant your heartfelt request and advance you with exalted honors.

sentences.zh: 尚齒優賢，斯王化之本也。

translations.literal: To honor age and prefer the worthy—this is the root of royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: To honor the aged and esteem the worthy is the foundation of sage rule.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫、守司徒、同中書門下平章事、兼充弘文館大學士、太清宮使、上柱國、岐國公、食邑三千戶杜佑，巖廊上才，邦國茂器；

translations.literal: Grand Minister of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Qi with a fief of three thousand households—Du You: a top talent of the state hall, a lush vessel of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Du You—Grand Minister of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Minister of Works, Chancellor, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Qi with a fief of three thousand households—a towering talent of the court and a treasure of the state;

sentences.zh: 蘊經通之識，履溫厚之姿，寬裕本乎性情，謀猷彰乎事業。

translations.literal: He contains penetrating knowledge of the classics, treads a warm and generous bearing; magnanimity stems from his nature, strategies shine in his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His learning penetrates the classics; his bearing is warm and generous; magnanimity is native to him and his counsel has marked every office he held.

sentences.zh: 博聞強學，知歷代沿革之宜；

translations.literal: Broadly heard, strongly learned—he knows the fitness of each dynasty's evolution;
translations.idiomatic: Widely learned, he understands what each age required in institutional change;

sentences.zh: 為政惠人，審群黎利病之要。

translations.literal: In governing he benefits the people, scrutinizing the essentials of popular gain and harm.
translations.idiomatic: In government he has served the people, discerning what harms or helps the masses.

sentences.zh: 由是再司邦用，累歷籓方，出總戎麾，入和鼎實，聿膺重寄，歷事先朝，左右朕躬，夙夜不懈。

translations.literal: Hence twice managing state revenue, repeatedly passing through provinces, going out to oversee military staffs and entering to harmonize the tripods—he has shouldered heavy trust, served the prior court, aided the emperor at left and right, diligent from dawn to dusk without slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he directed national finance and served repeatedly in the provinces; whether commanding armies or harmonizing the central government he bore the throne's weightiest trust, served the previous emperor, and attended the present sovereign night and day without slackening.

sentences.zh: 命以詔冊，登之上公，肅恭在廷，華發承弁。

translations.literal: Ordered by edict and book, raised to the Grand Excellency, reverent in the hall, white hair wearing the cap.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial decree he was raised to Grand Excellency; white-haired, he stands in court with reverent dignity.

sentences.zh: 茲可謂國之元老，人之具瞻者也。

translations.literal: This may be called the state's elder statesman, one upon whom all gaze.
translations.idiomatic: He is truly the state's elder statesman and a man all look up to.

sentences.zh: 朕纘承丕業，思弘景化，選勞求舊，期致時邕，方伸引翼之儀，遽抗懸車之請。

translations.literal: I have inherited the great enterprise, thinking to expand the splendid transformation, selecting the weary and seeking the old, expecting to reach timely harmony—just as wing-supporting ceremony was to be extended, suddenly resisting the request to hang up the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the great enterprise I seek to broaden our glorious age, honoring worn veterans in hope of universal peace—yet just as I meant to lean upon you further, you urgently plead to hang up your carriage and retire.

sentences.zh: 而又固辭年疾，乞就休閑，已而復來，星琯屢變，有不可抑，良用耿然。

translations.literal: Moreover he firmly declines on grounds of age and illness, begging to take leisure; already he has returned, then stars and seasons have repeatedly changed; there is what cannot be suppressed—a bitter feeling stirs.
translations.idiomatic: You again insist on illness and beg for leisure; time and again you have returned only to withdraw as the seasons turn, and what cannot be denied finally moves us to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 永惟古先哲王，君臣之際，臣有耆艾以求其退，君有優賜以徇其情；

translations.literal: Ever reflecting on the ancient sage kings, at the juncture of lord and minister—the minister has elder worth to seek his withdrawal, the lord has preferential bestowal to indulge his feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the ancient sages in the relation of ruler and subject, the minister in his age seeks release and the ruler in kindness grants his wish;

sentences.zh: 乃輟鄧禹敷教之功，仍增王祥輔導之秩，俾養浩然之氣，安於敬止之鄉，庶乎怡神葆和，永綏福履。

translations.literal: Thus we pause Deng Yu's achievement in spreading instruction, yet still add Wang Xiang's rank in assisting guidance, causing him to nourish vast and vigorous qi, secure in the village of reverent stopping—perhaps he will ease the spirit and preserve harmony, forever securing fortune's tread.
translations.idiomatic: we pause the active duties you once bore like Deng Yu, yet grant you the honored rank of a Wang Xiang, that you may nourish your spirit in dignified repose, find ease in body and mind, and enjoy lasting fortune.

sentences.zh: 仍加階級，以厚寵章，可光祿大夫、守太保致仕，宜朝朔望。

translations.literal: Still adding rank and grade to thicken the favor's seal—he may be Grand Minister of the Gold Seal, Acting Grand Mentor in retirement, and should attend court on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: We further raise your rank to seal this honor: you are appointed Grand Minister of the Gold Seal, Acting Grand Mentor with retirement status, and shall attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 是日，上遣中使就佑第賜絹五百匹、錢五百千。

translations.literal: That day the emperor sent a palace envoy to You's residence to bestow five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor sent an imperial envoy to Du You's house with five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月薨，壽七十八，廢朝三日，冊贈太傅，謚曰安簡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he died; his years reached seventy-eight; court was suspended three days; enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Tutor; posthumous title Anjian (Peaceful and Concise).
translations.idiomatic: He died that November at seventy-eight; court mourning lasted three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor with the title Anjian.

sentences.zh: 佑性敦厚強力，尤精吏職，雖外示寬和，而持身有術。

translations.literal: You's nature was sincere and thick, strong and forceful; he especially mastered clerkly duties; though outwardly he showed lenience and harmony, in holding himself there was method.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was sincere, forceful, and especially skilled at bureaucratic administration; though he appeared mild, he governed himself with shrewd discipline.

sentences.zh: 為政弘易，不尚皦察，掌計治民，物便而濟，馭戎應變，即非所長。

translations.literal: In governing he was broad and easy, not exalting minute inspection; in managing accounts and ordering the people, things were convenient and affairs went smoothly; directing troops and responding to change—that was not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: His government was broad and easy rather than finicky; in finance and civil administration he made things work efficiently, but command of troops and crisis response were not his strengths.

sentences.zh: 性嗜學，該涉古今，以富國安人之術為己任。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning, covered ancient and modern comprehensively, and took methods to enrich the state and settle the people as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, ranged widely through history, and made enriching the state and comforting the people his life's work.

sentences.zh: 初開元末，劉秩采經史百家之言，取《周禮》六官所職，撰分門書三十五卷，號曰《政典》，大為時賢稱賞；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the late Kaiyuan, Liu Zhi gathered words from the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, took the duties of the six offices in the "Rites of Zhou," and compiled a classified book of thirty-five volumes called "Administrative Canon," greatly praised by the worthies of the time;
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kaiyuan era Liu Zhi assembled classical and historical learning, drew on the six ministries of the "Rites of Zhou," and compiled thirty-five classified volumes called the "Administrative Canon," which the learned greatly admired;

sentences.zh: 房琯以為才過劉更生。

translations.literal: Fang Guan thought his talent surpassed Liu Gengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan judged him superior to Liu Xin.

sentences.zh: 佑得其書，尋味厥旨，以為條目未盡，因而廣之，加以開元禮、樂，書成二百卷，號曰《通典》。

translations.literal: You obtained his book, savored its aim, thought the entries not complete, and accordingly expanded it, adding Kaiyuan rites and music; when the book was finished it was two hundred volumes, called "Comprehensive Institutions."
translations.idiomatic: Du You studied the work, found its categories incomplete, expanded it with Kaiyuan ritual and music codes, and produced two hundred volumes titled the "Comprehensive Institutions."

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年，自淮南使人詣闕獻之，曰：

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan, from Huainan he sent a man to the capital to present it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 801, from his post in Huainan he sent an envoy to the capital to present it, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞太上立德，不可庶幾；

translations.literal: Your subject hears that the highest establishes virtue—it cannot be approached;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the highest attainments establish virtue beyond reach;

sentences.zh: 其次立功，遂行當代；

translations.literal: next, establishing achievement that is then carried out in the age;
translations.idiomatic: next, establishing deeds that shape the age;

sentences.zh: 其次立言，見誌後學。

translations.literal: next, establishing words to leave records for later students.
translations.idiomatic: next, establishing words to guide posterity.

sentences.zh: 由是往哲遞相祖述，將施有政，用乂邦家。

translations.literal: Hence past sages handed down in succession, intending to apply governance and use it to govern the state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Thus sages through the ages transmitted their learning so that policy might order state and clan.

sentences.zh: 臣本以門資，幼登官序，仕非遊藝，才不逮人，徒懷自強，頗玩墳籍。

translations.literal: Your subject originally by family qualification, as a youth entered the official sequence; service was not wandering in arts; talent did not reach others'; vainly cherishing self-strengthening, I rather played in tomb books.
translations.idiomatic: I entered office by family privilege, not by literary fame; my talent was no match for others', yet I strove to improve myself and pored over the classics.
