sentences.zh: 雖履歷叨幸，或職劇務殷，竊惜光陰，未嘗輕廢。

translations.literal: Though my record of posts has been fortunate, at times duties were acute and affairs many—I secretly treasured time and never lightly discarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortune raised me to heavy offices, I never lightly squandered an hour of study.

sentences.zh: 夫《孝經》、《尚書》、《毛詩》、《周易》、《三傳》，皆父子君臣之要道；

translations.literal: Now the "Classic of Filial Piety," "Documents," "Mao Odes," "Changes," and the "Three Commentaries" are all essentials of father-son and lord-minister;
translations.idiomatic: The "Classic of Filial Piety," "Documents," "Mao Odes," "Changes," and the Three Commentaries all teach the duties of ruler and subject, father and son;

sentences.zh: 十倫五教之宏綱，如日月之下臨，天地之大德，百王是式，終古攸遵。

translations.literal: the great warp of the ten relationships and five teachings—like the sun and moon looking down, heaven and earth's great virtue; the hundred kings take it as model, from antiquity to the end one follows it.
translations.idiomatic: they are the great fabric of human relations, bright as sun and moon, vast as heaven and earth; every ruler has taken them as model through all time.

sentences.zh: 然多記言，罕存法制；

translations.literal: Yet they mostly record words and rarely preserve institutions and laws;
translations.idiomatic: Yet they chiefly record teachings and seldom set forth institutional law.

sentences.zh: 愚管窺測，莫達高深，輒肆荒虛，誠為億度。

translations.literal: This foolish tube peeping and measuring cannot reach the high and deep; I rashly venture into wild emptiness—it is truly a hundred million reckonings.
translations.idiomatic: My narrow vision cannot plumb their depths; what I dare present is presumptuous guesswork beyond count.

sentences.zh: 每念懵學，莫探政經，略觀歷代眾賢著論，多陳紊失之弊，或闕匡拯之方。

translations.literal: Whenever I think of dull learning, not probing the warp of government—briefly viewing the worthies of each age who authored treatises, many state the ills of disorder and loss, or lack methods of rescue and support.
translations.idiomatic: Conscious of my ignorance of statecraft, I read the treatises of past worthies, most of which expose disorders without offering remedies.

sentences.zh: 臣既庸淺，寧詳損益，未原其始，莫暢其終。

translations.literal: Your subject is already mediocre and shallow—how can I detail gain and loss? I have not traced things to the beginning nor made their end clear.
translations.idiomatic: I am too shallow to weigh every gain and loss from origin to end.

sentences.zh: 尚賴周氏典禮，秦皇蕩滅不盡，縱有繁雜，且用準繩。

translations.literal: Still relying on the Zhou clan's canonical rites—the First Emperor of Qin swept yet did not extinguish them entirely; though there is complexity, for now we take them as the plumb line.
translations.idiomatic: Still we have the Zhou rituals, not wholly destroyed by the First Emperor of Qin; cumbersome though they are, they serve as a standard.

sentences.zh: 至於往昔是非，可為來今龜鏡，布在方冊，亦粗研尋。

translations.literal: As for past right and wrong, they can be a tortoise mirror for what is to come; spread in registers—I have also roughly researched them.
translations.idiomatic: Past successes and failures can mirror the future; spread through the archives, I have studied them as well as I could.

sentences.zh: 自頃纘修，年逾三紀，識寡思拙，心昧辭蕪。

translations.literal: From recently continuing the compilation, years have passed three decades; knowledge scant, thought clumsy, heart dim, words overgrown.
translations.idiomatic: In compiling this work more than thirty years have passed; my mind is dull and my prose rough.

sentences.zh: 圖籍實多，事目非少，將事功畢，罔愧乖疏，固不足發揮大猷，但竭愚盡慮而已。

translations.literal: Documents are truly many, item headings not few; when the work is finished I will not be ashamed of gaps and errors—truly insufficient to display great design, only exhausting stupidity and exhausting thought.
translations.idiomatic: The sources are vast and the topics countless; when the task is done I cannot escape flaws, for I have no grand design, only the exhaustion of a fool's effort.

sentences.zh: 書凡九門，計貳百卷，不敢不具上獻，庶明鄙誌所之，塵瀆聖聰，兢惶無措。

translations.literal: The book in all has nine gates, totaling two hundred volumes—I dare not fail to present it fully, hoping to clarify my humble aim; dust defiles the sage hearing—I am fearful beyond recourse.
translations.idiomatic: The book has nine sections and two hundred volumes; I dare not withhold it and hope it shows my humble purpose, though I tremble at troubling your sacred ear.

sentences.zh: 優詔嘉之，命藏書府。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised it; he was ordered to store it in the book repository.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised it and ordered it deposited in the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 其書大傳於時，禮樂刑政之源，千載如指諸掌，大為士君子所稱。

translations.literal: His book greatly circulated at the time; the source of rites, music, punishments, and government—for a thousand years it was like pointing at the palm; it was greatly praised by gentlemen and scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The work spread widely; for a millennium the roots of ritual, music, punishment, and government lay in the hand like the lines of a palm, and scholars everywhere praised it.

sentences.zh: 佑性勤而無倦，雖位極將相，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: You's nature was diligent without weariness; though his rank reached general and minister, his hand did not release the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was tireless in study; though he reached the summit of power he never put down a book.

sentences.zh: 質明視事，接對賓客，夜則燈下讀書，孜孜不怠。

translations.literal: At dawn he attended to business and received guests; at night by lamplight he read books, earnest and untiring.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he handled affairs and received guests; by lamp at night he read on without slackening.

sentences.zh: 與賓佐談論，人憚其辯而伏其博，設有疑誤，亦能質正。

translations.literal: In discussion with guests and aides, people feared his eloquence yet submitted to his breadth; should there be doubt or error, he could also question and correct.
translations.idiomatic: In debate with staff he intimidated by argument yet won them by learning; when they erred he corrected them plainly.

sentences.zh: 始終言行，無所玷缺，唯在淮南時，妻梁氏亡後，升嬖妾李氏為正室，封密國夫人，親族子弟言之不從，時論非之。

translations.literal: From beginning to end in words and conduct there was no stain or lack—only when at Huainan, after his wife the Lady Liang died, he raised the concubine Lady Li as principal wife, enfeoffed her Dame of the State of Mi; kin and younger kin spoke but he did not follow; contemporary opinion criticized it.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was otherwise without blemish, save that in Huainan, after Lady Liang died, he made his concubine Lady Li principal wife and enfeoffed her Dame of Mi—a step his kin urged against and public opinion condemned.

sentences.zh: 三子，師損嗣，位終司農少卿。

translations.literal: Three sons; Shisun succeeded him, ending rank as Vice Minister of Revenue for Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons; Shisun succeeded him and rose no higher than Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子 式方式方，字考元。

translations.literal: Son: Shifang (Du Shifang), styled Kaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du Shifang, styled Kaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 以廕授揚府參軍，轉常州晉陵尉。

translations.literal: By privilege appointed Yangzhou Secretariat aide; transferred to Jinling subprefect in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he became an aide in Yangzhou and later Jinling subprefect in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使王緯辟為從事，入為太子通事舍人，改太常寺主簿。

translations.literal: The Huai-West observation commissioner Wang Wei recruited him as aide; he entered as Crown Prince Communications Attendant, changed to Director of Records in the Grand Harmony Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, commissioner of Huai-Si, took him as aide; he then entered as Crown Prince Communications Attendant and became a director in the Grand Harmony Office.

sentences.zh: 明練鐘律，有所考定，深為高郢所賞。

translations.literal: He was bright and practiced in bells and pitch pipes, made some investigations and fixes, deeply prized by Gao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in pitch and measure, he made revisions in music that Gao Ying greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 時父作鎮揚州，家財鉅萬，甲第在安仁裏，杜城有別墅，亭館林池，為城南之最。

translations.literal: At the time his father was governing Yangzhou; family wealth was in the tens of thousands; a noble mansion was in Anren Lane; the Du clan had a separate villa outside the city—pavilions, halls, woods, and pools were the finest south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While his father governed Yangzhou the family wealth ran to millions; their mansion in Anren Lane and country villa beyond the walls were the grandest estates south of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 昆仲皆在朝廷，與時賢遊從，樂而有節。

translations.literal: Brothers all were in the court, associating with the worthies of the time—joyful yet regulated.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers all held court office and moved among leading scholars with pleasure but without excess.

sentences.zh: 既而佑入中書，出為昭應令。

translations.literal: Before long You entered the Central Secretariat; he went out as magistrate of Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Du You entered the Secretariat, Shifang was posted magistrate of Zhaoying.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，遷司農少卿，賜金紫，加正議大夫、太仆卿。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning, when mourning ended he was transferred Vice Minister of Revenue for Agriculture, granted the gold seal and purple ribbon, added Regular Grandee and Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, given the gold seal and purple, and named Regular Grandee and Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 時少子悰選尚公主，式方以右戚移病不視事。

translations.literal: At the time the youngest son Cong was selected to marry a princess; Shifang on account of close kin feigned illness and did not attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: When his youngest brother Cong was chosen to marry a princess, Shifang pleaded illness and withdrew from office rather than serve amid such nepotism.

sentences.zh: 久之，穆宗即位，轉兼御史中丞，充桂管觀察都防禦使。

translations.literal: After a long while Muzong took the throne; he was transferred concurrently to Censor-in-chief, and appointed Governing Commissioner and Overall Defender of Guizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, when Muzong ascended, he was made Censor-in-chief and commissioner of Guizhou with full defensive powers.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年三月，卒於位，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Changqing he died in office; posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in March 822 and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 式方性孝友，弟兄尤睦。

translations.literal: Shifang's nature was filial and friendly; with brothers he was especially harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang was filial and deeply devoted to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 季弟從郁，少多疾病，式方每躬自煎調，藥膳水飲，非經式方之手，不入於口。

translations.literal: His younger brother Congyu in youth had many illnesses; Shifang every time personally decocted and adjusted—medicine, food, and water—what had not passed through Shifang's hand did not enter the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Congyu was often ill; Shifang personally prepared every medicine, meal, and drink, and nothing passed Congyu's lips unless Shifang had touched it.

sentences.zh: 及從郁夭喪，終年號泣，殆不勝情，士友多之。

translations.literal: When Congyu died young, for a whole year he wailed; nearly unable to bear feeling—gentlemen and friends greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After Congyu's early death he mourned aloud for a year, grief nearly beyond bearing, and friends greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 子惲、憓、悰、恂。

translations.literal: Sons: Yun, Hui, Cong, Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yun, Hui, Cong, and Xun.

sentences.zh: 惲嗣，富平尉；

translations.literal: Yun succeeded him, Fuping subprefect;
translations.idiomatic: Yun succeeded him as subprefect of Fuping;

sentences.zh: 憓，興平尉。

translations.literal: Hui, Xingping subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Hui served as subprefect of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 式方子 悰悰，以廕三遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Du Shifang's son: Cong (Du Cong), by privilege thrice promoted to Crown Prince Ceremonial Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shifang's son Du Cong entered office by privilege and after three steps became Crown Prince Ceremonial Reviewer.

sentences.zh: 元和九年，選尚公主，召見於麟德殿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe, selected to marry a princess, summoned to audience in Qilin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 814 he was chosen to marry a princess and summoned before the throne in Qilin Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋尚岐陽公主，加銀青光祿大夫、殿中少監、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Soon he married Princess Qiyang, added Grand Minister of the Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon, Palace Vice Director, and Chief Commandant for the Imperial Son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He soon wed Princess Qiyang, becoming Grand Minister of the Silver Seal, Palace Vice Director, and Chief Commandant for Imperial Sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 岐陽，憲宗長女，郭妃之所生。

translations.literal: Qiyang was Xianzong's eldest daughter, born of Consort Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyang was Xianzong's eldest daughter by Consort Guo.

sentences.zh: 自頃選尚，多於貴戚，或武臣節將之家。

translations.literal: From recent selections for marriage, many were from noble kin, or homes of martial ministers and frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: For some time princesses had been married chiefly into noble houses or families of generals.

sentences.zh: 於時翰林學士獨孤郁，權德輿之女婿，時德輿作相，郁避嫌辭內職。

translations.literal: At the time the Hanlin academician Dugu Yu was son-in-law to Quan Deyu; as Deyu was then chancellor, Yu avoided suspicion and resigned his inner-office post.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin scholar Dugu Yu was son-in-law to Quan Deyu; when Deyu became chancellor Yu resigned his inner post to avoid suspicion.

sentences.zh: 上頗重學士，不獲已許之，且嘆德輿有佳婿，遂令宰臣於卿士家選尚文雅之士可居清列者。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued academicians and had no choice but to permit it; moreover he sighed that Deyu had a fine son-in-law, then ordered the ministers from scholar-official houses to select a refined gentleman fit for a pure court rank to marry in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his scholars and reluctantly assented, praising Deyu's son-in-law and directing his ministers to choose among cultivated gentlemen of good families for the marriage.

sentences.zh: 初於文學後進中選擇，皆辭疾不應，唯悰願焉。

translations.literal: At first among literary juniors they chose—all declined illness and did not respond; only Cong was willing.
translations.idiomatic: They first offered it to promising scholars of letters, all of whom pleaded illness, until only Cong accepted.

sentences.zh: 累遷至司農卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue for Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，轉京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he was transferred Magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In 832 he became magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 七年，檢校刑部尚書，出為鳳翔尹、鳳翔隴右節度。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Acting Minister of Punishments, he went out as Magistrate of Fengxiang and military commissioner of Fengxiang Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In 833 he was made Acting Minister of Punishments and posted as magistrate and military commissioner of Fengxiang in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，八年，起復授忠武軍節度使、陳許蔡觀察等使，就加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On inner-court mourning, in the eighth year he was recalled from mourning to be military commissioner of Zhongwu Army and observation commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Cai, and was thereupon added Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning within the clan he was recalled in 838 as commissioner of Zhongwu and Chen-Xu-Cai, with concurrent appointment as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 開成初，入為工部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he entered as Minister of Works and judged revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaicheng he entered as Minister of Works with charge of revenue.

sentences.zh: 屬岐陽公主薨，久而未謝。

translations.literal: As Princess Qiyang died, for a long time he did not present thanks for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Qiyang died he long delayed reporting back for duty.

sentences.zh: 文宗怪之，問左右。

translations.literal: Wenzong thought it strange and asked those at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong wondered at this and asked his attendants.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎李玨對曰：「近日駙馬為公主服斬衰三年，所以士族之家不願為國戚者，半為此也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jue replied: "Recently imperial sons-in-law wore hemp mourning for princesses for three years—hence scholar families are unwilling to become imperial affines: half is for this.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jue answered: "Of late sons-in-law have worn the deepest mourning for a princess for three years—that is why eminent families shun marriage to the throne, and this is half the reason.

sentences.zh: 杜悰未謝，拘此服紀也。」

translations.literal: Du Cong has not presented thanks, bound by this mourning regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong has not reported back because he is held by this mourning rule.

sentences.zh: 上愕然曰：「予初不知。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in astonishment: "I did not know at first."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed in surprise: "I never knew.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「制服輕重，必由典禮。

translations.literal: Then an edict said: "The weight of mourning garments must follow canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "The weight of mourning must follow canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 如聞往者駙馬為公主服三年，緣情之義，殊非故實，違經之制，今乃聞知。

translations.literal: As I hear, in the past imperial sons-in-law mourned princesses for three years—by the meaning of feeling, this is especially not the old reality, a system violating the classics—only now do I hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: I learn that sons-in-law have lately mourned princesses three years—a kindness beyond precedent and a breach of the classics, which I knew nothing of until now.

sentences.zh: 宜令行杖周，永為通制。」

translations.literal: They should be ordered to perform the full week's ritual and make it a standing regulation forever."
translations.idiomatic: Let them observe only a week's mourning hereafter, and let this be the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 三年，改戶部尚書，兼判戶部度支事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Minister of Revenue and concurrently judged revenue affairs of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the ministry's revenue accounts.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，尋加左僕射。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director, soon added Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang he became Vice Director and Associate Director of the Secretariat, soon added Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 大中初，出鎮西川，降先沒吐蕃維州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he went out to govern Xichuan and received the surrender of Weizhou, formerly lost to the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong he was sent to govern Sichuan and accepted the surrender of Weizhou, long held by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 州即古西戎地也，其地南界江陽，岷山連嶺而西，不知其極；

translations.literal: The prefecture is ancient Western Rong territory; its land borders Jiangyang to the south; Min Mountains connect in ridges to the west, their limit unknown;
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was ancient western borderland; south it bordered Jiangyang and westward the Min ranges stretched beyond sight;

sentences.zh: 北望隴山，積雪如玉：東望成都，若在井底。

translations.literal: north looking to Long Mountains, snow piled like jade; east looking to Chengdu, as if at the bottom of a well.
translations.idiomatic: northward Long Mountains rose white with snow; eastward Chengdu seemed to lie at the bottom of a well.

sentences.zh: 地接石紐山，夏禹生於石紐山是也。

translations.literal: The ground connects to Stone Knob Mountain—it is where the Great Yu of Xia was born at Stone Knob Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: It adjoins Stone Knob Mountain, said to be where Yu of Xia was born.

sentences.zh: 其州在岷山之孤峰，三面臨江。

translations.literal: The prefecture stands on a lone peak of the Min Mountains, three sides facing the river.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on a solitary Min peak with river on three sides.

sentences.zh: 天寶後，河、隴繼陷，惟此州在焉。

translations.literal: After Tianbao, the Yellow River region and Longyou fell in succession; only this prefecture remained.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianbao the Hexi and Longyou regions fell one by one, yet this prefecture alone held.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃利其險要，二十年間，設計得之，遂據其城，因號曰「無憂城」，吐蕃由是不虞邛、蜀之兵。

translations.literal: The Tibetans coveted its strategic strength; within twenty years they schemed and obtained it, then held its walls, and so called it "Carefree City"—from this the Tibetans no longer guarded against Qiong and Shu troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet prized its terrain; within twenty years they schemed and took it, named it "Carefree City," and no longer feared armies from Qiong and Shu.

sentences.zh: 先是，李德裕鎮西川，維州吐蕃首領悉怛謀以城來降，德裕奏之；

translations.literal: Before this, Li Deyu governed Xichuan; the Weizhou Tibetan leader Xin Dangnu offered the city in surrender; Deyu memorialized it;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Li Deyu governed Sichuan, the Tibetan leader of Weizhou, Xin Dangnu, offered the city in surrender and Deyu reported it to court;

sentences.zh: 執政者與德裕不協，遽勒還其城。

translations.literal: Those administering government were not in harmony with Deyu; they hastily ordered the city returned.
translations.idiomatic: The men in power were at odds with Li Deyu and quickly ordered Weizhou handed back.

sentences.zh: 至是復收之，亦不因兵刃，乃人情所歸也。

translations.literal: At this time they recovered it again, yet not through blades of war—it was where human feeling inclined.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was taken again, yet without a blow struck; the people themselves had turned toward the court.

sentences.zh: 俄復入相，加司空，繼加司徒，歷鎮重籓。

translations.literal: Soon he again entered the council; he was made Minister of Works, then Minister of Education, and in turn governed weighty border commands.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was back in the council, made Minister of Works and then Minister of Education, and served in turn at major frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 至是加太傅、邠國公。

translations.literal: At this time he was made Grand Tutor and Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he was made Grand Tutor and Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 悰無他才，常延接寒素，甘食竊位而已。

translations.literal: Cong had no other talent; he constantly received poor scholars of humble birth—sweet eating and usurped office, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had no other gifts; he merely welcomed poor scholars, ate well, and held a post he did not deserve—that was all.

sentences.zh: 式方季弟 從郁從郁，以廕貞元末再遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Shifang's youngest brother: Cong Yu (Cong Yu), by privilege at the end of Zhenyuan again promoted to Crown Prince Ceremonial Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang's youngest brother Cong Yu entered office by privilege and, late in Zhenyuan, was again promoted to Crown Prince Ceremonial Reviewer.

sentences.zh: 元和初，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he was transferred to Left Remonstrance Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he became Left Remonstrance Councillor.

sentences.zh: 諫官崔群、韋貫之、獨孤郁等以從郁宰相子，不合為諫官，乃降授左拾遺。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Cui Qun, Wei Guanzhi, Dugu Yu, and others, because Cong Yu was a chancellor's son, held it improper to be remonstrance officials; he was therefore demoted and appointed Left Collector of Lost Writings.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officials Cui Qun, Wei Guanzhi, and Dugu Yu argued that as a chancellor's son Cong Yu should not sit in the remonstrance ranks, and he was demoted to Left Collector of Lost Writings.

sentences.zh: 群等復執曰：「拾遺之與補闕，雖資品有殊，皆名諫列。

translations.literal: Qun and the others again pressed, saying: "Between Collector of Lost Writings and Remonstrance Councillor, though rank and grade differ, both are named in the remonstrance roster.
translations.idiomatic: Qun and his colleagues pressed again: "Collector and Remonstrance Councillor differ in rank, yet both belong to the remonstrance roster.

sentences.zh: 父為宰相，子為諫官，若政有得失，不可使子論父。」

translations.literal: The father is chancellor, the son a remonstrance official—if government has gain or loss, one cannot have the son discuss the father."
translations.idiomatic: When the father is chancellor and the son a remonstrance officer, the son cannot be allowed to judge his father's policies.

sentences.zh: 乃改為秘書丞，終駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was therefore changed to Secretariat Assistant and ended as Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Secretariat Assistant and ended his career as Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 從郁子 顗子牧、顗，俱登進士第。

translations.literal: Cong Yu's sons: Yan; Mu and Yan both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Yu's sons Yan and Mu both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 顗後病目而卒。

translations.literal: Yan later fell ill in the eyes and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan later went blind and died.

sentences.zh: 從郁子 牧牧，字牧之，既以進士擢第，又制舉登乙第，解褐弘文館校書郎，試左武衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Cong Yu's son: Mu (Mu), styled Muzhi; having passed the jinshi and been selected, he also passed the special examination at second grade; he left the cloth and became Collator at the Hongwen Institute, tried as Military Staff Officer of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Yu's son Du Mu, styled Muzhi, won the jinshi and also placed second in the special examination; he left private life as collator at the Hongwen Institute and served provisionally as military staff officer of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 沈傳師廉察江西宣州，辟牧為從事、試大理評事。

translations.literal: Shen Chuanshi inspected Jiangxi and Xuanzhou and recruited Mu as aide, tried as Grand Court Evaluator.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Chuanshi inspected Jiangxi and Xuanzhou he took Mu on as aide and acting Grand Court Evaluator.

sentences.zh: 又為淮南節度推官、監察御史裏行，轉掌書記。

translations.literal: He also served as Huainan circuit staff officer, Acting Investigating Censor, and was transferred to chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the Huainan staff as acting investigating censor and then chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 俄真拜監察御史，分司東都，以弟顗病目棄官。

translations.literal: Soon he was truly appointed Investigating Censor, with a detached post in the Eastern Capital; because his brother Yan's eyes were diseased he abandoned office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was formally made investigating censor with a detached post at the eastern capital, but quit when his brother Yan went blind.

sentences.zh: 授宣州團練判官、殿中侍御史、內供奉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Xuanzhou training commissioner judge, Palace Attending Censor, and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judge on the Xuanzhou training commission, palace attending censor, and inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷左補闕、史館修撰，轉膳部、比部員外郎，並兼史職。

translations.literal: He was moved to Left Remonstrance Councillor and Historiography Compiler, transferred to Vice Director of Provisions and Vice Director of Accounts, both concurrently holding historiographical duty.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Remonstrance Councillor and historiography compiler, then vice director of provisions and of accounts, keeping his historiographical duties throughout.

sentences.zh: 出牧黃、池、睦三郡，復遷司勛員外郎、史館修撰，轉吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He went out to govern the three prefectures Huang, Chi, and Mu; again he was moved to Vice Director of Merits, Historiography Compiler, and transferred to Vice Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Huang, Chi, and Mu in turn, then returned as vice director of merits and historiography compiler and finally vice director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 又以弟病免歸。

translations.literal: Again because of his brother's illness he was excused and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Again he resigned and went home when his brother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 授湖州刺史，入拜考功郎中、知制誥，歲中遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Huzhou; he entered court as Director of Evaluations and Drafted Edicts; within the year he was moved to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Huzhou, then summoned as director of evaluations with charge of edicts, and within the year promoted to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 牧好讀書，工詩為文，嘗自負經緯才略。

translations.literal: Mu loved reading books, was skilled in poetry and prose, and once prided himself on statecraft and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Mu loved books, excelled at poetry and prose, and prided himself on statecraft and strategy.

sentences.zh: 武宗朝誅昆夷、鮮卑，牧上宰相書論兵事，言「胡戎入寇，在秋冬之間，盛夏無備，宜五六月中擊胡為便」。

translations.literal: In the Wuzong reign Kunyi and Xianbei were executed; Mu sent the chancellor a letter discussing military affairs, saying: "When the Hu barbarians invade, it is between autumn and winter; in high summer they are unprepared—striking the Hu in the fifth or sixth month is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: During Wuzong's campaign against the Kunyi and Xianbei, Mu wrote the chancellor on military affairs, arguing that barbarian raids came in autumn and winter, that they were unready in midsummer, and that the fifth or sixth month was the best time to strike.

sentences.zh: 李德裕稱之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 註曹公所定《孫武十三篇》行於代。

translations.literal: He annotated Lord Cao's fixed "Thirteen Chapters of Sun Wu," which circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary on Cao Cao's recension of Sunzi's Thirteen Chapters circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 牧從兄悰隆盛於時，牧居下位，心常不樂。

translations.literal: Mu's cousin Cong was flourishing at the time; Mu dwelt in lower rank and his heart was constantly unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Du Cong was at the height of power while Mu languished in lesser posts, and the contrast rankled him.

sentences.zh: 將及知命，得病，自為墓誌、祭文。

translations.literal: As he neared the age of knowing fate he fell ill and composed his own tomb inscription and sacrificial text.
translations.idiomatic: Approaching fifty he fell ill and wrote his own epitaph and funeral ode.

sentences.zh: 又嘗夢人告曰：「爾改名畢。」

translations.literal: He also once dreamed a man telling him: "Your renaming is finished."
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed a man telling him, "Your renaming is complete.

sentences.zh: 逾月，奴自家來，告曰：「炊將熟而甑裂。」

translations.literal: After a month a slave came from home and reported: "The rice is nearly cooked but the steamer cracked."
translations.idiomatic: A month later a servant from home reported, "The rice was nearly done when the steamer split.

sentences.zh: 牧曰：「皆不祥也。」

translations.literal: Mu said: "All are inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Mu said, "All of these are ill omens.

sentences.zh: 俄又夢書行紙曰：「皎皎白駒，在彼空谷。」

translations.literal: Soon he again dreamed writing on moving paper: "Bright bright the white colt, in that empty valley."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he dreamed words written on drifting paper: "Bright, bright the white colt, there in the empty valley.

sentences.zh: 寤寢而嘆曰：「此過隙也。

translations.literal: Waking from sleep he sighed: "This is a passing shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Waking, he sighed, "This is life's brief gap.

sentences.zh: 吾生於角，徵還於角，為第八宮，吾之甚厄也。

translations.literal: I was born in Jiao; Zhi returns to Jiao—it is the eighth palace; my great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I was born under the Horn; Fire returns to the Horn in the eighth palace—my gravest misfortune.

sentences.zh: 予自湖守遷舍人，木還角，足矣。」

translations.literal: I from Huzhou prefect moved to drafter—wood returns to Horn; it is enough."
translations.idiomatic: From Huzhou prefect to secretariat drafter, Wood returns to the Horn—that is enough for me.

sentences.zh: 其年，以疾終於安仁裏，年五十。

translations.literal: That year, through illness he ended at Anren Lane, age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died of illness at Anren Lane, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，曰《杜氏樊川集》，行於代。

translations.literal: He had a collection of twenty scrolls, called "Du Clan Fanchuan Collection," circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left a twenty-scroll collection called the Du Clan Fanchuan Collection, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子德祥，官至丞郎。

translations.literal: His son Dexiang reached office as a director and gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dexiang rose to a vice-ministerial post.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: The Historian's Comment
translations.idiomatic: The Historian's Comment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：黃裳以道致君，持誠奉主；

translations.literal: The historian says: Huangchang by the Way brought the ruler, held sincerity and served the lord;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Huangchang guided his ruler by the Way and served him with whole-hearted loyalty;

sentences.zh: 辨懷光之詐，罷全義之征。

translations.literal: he distinguished Huai'guang's deceit and halted the campaign against Quanyi.
translations.idiomatic: he exposed Li Huai'guang's treachery and stopped the campaign against Quanyi;

sentences.zh: 討賊辟之兇，舉無遺算；

translations.literal: he punished the rebel Zebi's violence, his plans leaving nothing out;
translations.idiomatic: he crushed the rebel Zebi without a plan left unused;

sentences.zh: 葬執誼之柩，豈曰不仁。

translations.literal: he buried Zhuyi's coffin—can one say he was not humane?
translations.idiomatic: and he buried Liu Zhuyi's remains—who would call that inhumane?

sentences.zh: 郢天縱之性，總丱之年，代父命於臨刑，孝也；

translations.literal: Ying had heaven-endowed nature; in the years of gathered childhood he took his father's place at the execution ground—this was filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: Ying was gifted by nature; as a child he took his father's place at the execution block—filial piety;

sentences.zh: 懷光之亂，王人被傷，撫巢父於賊庭，義也；

translations.literal: in Huai'guang's rebellion the royal people were wounded; he comforted Chao Fu in the rebel court—this was righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: in Huai'guang's revolt, when the throne's servants were struck down, he comforted Chao Fu in the rebel camp—righteousness;

sentences.zh: 抑浮濫之流，考藝文之士，盡搜幽滯，大變時風，正也；

translations.literal: he restrained the floating and excessive current, examined literary scholars, thoroughly searched the obscure and stagnant, greatly changed the fashion of the age—this was uprightness;
translations.idiomatic: he curbed the tide of mediocrity, tested men of letters, sought out the overlooked, and changed the temper of the age—uprightness;

sentences.zh: 保止足之名，辭榮辱之路，高避世利，遐躅昔賢，智也。

translations.literal: he preserved the name of knowing when to stop, declined the path of glory and disgrace, loftily avoided worldly profit, far followed ancient worthies—this was wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: he kept the name of knowing when enough was enough, turned from honor and shame, stood above worldly gain, and walked in the steps of sages of old—wisdom.

sentences.zh: 忠孝全矣，仁智備矣！

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety were complete; benevolence and wisdom were equipped!
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety were whole, benevolence and wisdom complete!

sentences.zh: 此二子者，皆臨大節而不可奪也。

translations.literal: These two men both faced great integrity and could not be wrested from it.
translations.idiomatic: Both men, when tested at the great hinge of fate, could not be turned aside.

sentences.zh: 佑承廕入仕，讞獄受知，博古該今，輸忠效用；

translations.literal: You entered office by privilege, gained recognition in prison cases, were broad in antiquity and comprehensive in the present, offered loyalty and took effect;
translations.idiomatic: You entered office by privilege, won notice in judging cases, mastered antiquity and the present age alike, and served with loyal effect;

sentences.zh: 位居極品，榮逮子孫，操修之報，不亦宜哉！

translations.literal: his rank reached the highest grade, glory reached sons and grandsons—the reward of cultivated conduct, is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: he rose to the highest rank and his glory reached his sons—was that not a fitting reward for a life well lived?

sentences.zh: 及其賓僚紊法，嬖妾受封，事重因循，難乎語於正矣！

translations.literal: When it came to his guest officials disordering law, favored concubines receiving enfeoffment, affairs heavy with routine—hard to speak of in terms of rectitude!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when his staff bent the law, his concubines received fiefs, and affairs dragged on by habit, how could one still call him upright?

sentences.zh: 牧之文章，悰之長厚，能否既異，才位不倫，命矣夫！

translations.literal: Mu's literary works, Cong's long-standing generosity—ability and inability already differed; talent and position were not of a kind—such is fate!
translations.idiomatic: Mu had literature, Cong had steady kindness; their gifts differed, their talents and posts did not match—such is fate!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：貞公壯節，臨難奮發。

translations.literal: Appraisal says: Duke Zhen's stalwart integrity, facing hardship and rousing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Duke Zhen's firm integrity blazed forth in hardship.

sentences.zh: 言行無玷，斯為明哲。

translations.literal: Words and conduct without stain—this is clear wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Words and deeds without stain—that is true wisdom.

sentences.zh: 戡亂阜俗，時泰位隆。

translations.literal: Quelling disorder and enriching custom, the age at peace and rank lofty.
translations.idiomatic: They quelled disorder and enriched the realm; in peaceful times they rose to eminence.

sentences.zh: 國之名臣，鄭公、岐公。

translations.literal: The state's famed ministers: Duke of Zheng and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Among the state's great ministers stand the Duke of Zheng and the Duke of Qi.
